- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast peak and introduce early mean-reversion slope.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model frequently underestimates downward moves; increase forecast sensitivity to recent low prices.
- Model tends to lag in recognizing sustained downward trends; add 1–2 day lag correction for downward momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates short-term volatility; smooth out extreme swings and anchor to 14-day moving average of history.
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model may ignore trend reversal; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment decay and price correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model underreacts to recovery; add early upward bias to forecast rebound phase.
